paragraphs.text: Pontotoc Middle School’s sixth-grade agriculture students filled two tubs with peppers and tomatoes in their final harvest of the season, the school reported Nov. 19. A second report on Nov. 20 described what those students are doing with leaves they collected on campus and at Trace State Park.

The garden work began in August. During the first three days of school, students cleared raised beds and tended tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers. Later that month, Mrs. Whitworth’s class planted eight tomato plants donated by the school librarian, Mrs. Mathews, and her husband.

For their leaf booklets, students record each tree’s common and scientific names. They also describe the shape of the leaf and its margin, or outer edge. Whitworth’s class draws on specimens from the school grounds as well as those collected on the sixth-grade science trip.

On that trip, students met park manager Josh Massey, Mississippi Museum of Natural Science biologist Deborah Wise and Mississippi Forestry Commission outreach officer Mike Crabb, among other presenters. The school’s October account says they explained how their jobs involve managing outdoor spaces, caring for forests and studying living things.
